target_customer: Independent vacation rental owners and small property managers
problem: Small rental owners needed a website, a shared availability calendar and distribution across booking sites without building it themselves.
business_model: B2B SaaS subscription, starting at $12 per month in 2012, later multi channel management software
product_category: Vacation rental website builder and property management software

founders.name: Jonathan Murray
previous_startups: Two earlier companies, both acquired (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Described as vacation rental operator based in the Reno Tahoe area.

founders.name: Mike Stachowiak
previous_startups: Three earlier startups with exits (per YC page)
founders.background_notes: Investor in companies including Zapier and Clever, per YC page.

technical_complexity.rationale: Launch product was a website generator with a calendar; later channel integrations with Airbnb, Vrbo and others added API work. Standard web engineering.

defensibility.rationale: Websites and listings are easy to replicate, but once owners run bookings and channels through the software, switching is painful.

takeover_risk_then.outcome: No incumbent copied it early; consolidation came later, with rival Guesty buying MyVR in April 2021.

market_need_then: YC and TechCrunch framed vacation rentals as an $85 billion industry in 2012 with small owners lacking simple tools; the founders ran rentals themselves.

branding.brand_signature: The open platform for the vacation rental industry tagline

brand_strength.rationale: Short exact match domain and trade press coverage, but the name is confusable with virtual reality and no community or brand assets were found.

pivots.from: Website builder and marketing for owners
pivots.to: Multi channel vacation rental management platform
pivots.why: Product expanded to sync listings across booking sites; date approximate and not stated by a source.

outcome_analysis: MyVR raised $1.4M after YC in 2012, expanded from websites into multi channel management, raised a $6.1M Series A led by True Ventures in 2017 for $7.5M total, and was bought by rival Guesty in April 2021 for an undisclosed price. Founders with operator and exit experience and modest capital produced a consolidation exit.
notes: Competitor search returned only 2015 and later vendor pages, so the founding era list is empty. CB Insights dates the Series A 2017-10 versus 2017-12 press release. The 2012 seed investor list is from the YC blog and TechCrunch headline. Pivot date is an approximation. Founded 2012 per YC, CB Insights says 2010.
